title: A family of second-order methods for convex ℓ1-regularized optimization
contribution: A semi-smooth Newton framework that generates block active-set, orthant-based and second-order ISTA methods for convex f + ℓ1, plus a new active-set method with multiple active-manifold changes and an estimate-correction mechanism, compared numerically (abstract, 2012 OO preprint).
problem_entry: Minimize a convex f plus an ℓ1 regularization term, using second-order information about f to accelerate convergence (abstract).
key_idea: One semi-smooth Newton framework generates several second-order method classes; a new active-set method makes multiple changes to the active-manifold estimate and corrects estimates when needed; the corrective mechanism is also tried in an orthant-based method (abstract).
assumptions: Convex f; ℓ1 regularization (abstract). Smoothness and regularity assumptions not read.
experiments: Numerical tests comparing several second-order methods; test set and measures not read (abstract).
positioning: Posted to Optimization Online 2012/06/26 as a Northwestern Optimization Center tech report (June 2012); journal version Math. Program. 159 (2016), online 30 Nov 2015, 46 references (OO page; Crossref).

method_links.note: The estimate-correction component is evaluated in two method classes (active-set and orthant-based).
A recovery path for the active-manifold estimate (correcting estimates when needed), outside the noise setting; the trigger is not stated in the abstract.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: generating framework for a method family
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Semi-smooth Newton used as one generator of block active-set, orthant-based and second-order iterative soft-thresholding methods, then compared numerically.

transferable: Present rival method classes as instances of one generating framework, then transplant your new component into a second member of the family to test whether it is generic (abstract).
coauthors: Richard H. Byrd, Gillian M. Chin, Figen Oztoprak

quotes.text: We describe a semi-smooth Newton framework that can be used to generate a variety of second-order methods, including block active-set methods, orthant-based methods and a second-order iterative soft-thresholding method.
We also propose a new active set method that performs multiple changes in the active manifold estimate, and incorporates a novel mechanism for correcting estimates, when needed.

title: Collaborative Research: Algorithms for Large-Scale Stochastic and Nonlinear Optimization
contribution: NSF award DMS-1620022 (2016-2020, Nocedal sole PI on the record) for stochastic/batch hybrid algorithms for machine learning (gradient aggregation, adaptive sampling) with curvature information robust to inaccurate gradients; its outcomes report credits a progressive batching method and gradient-estimation quasi-Newton DFO (abstract; NSF outcomes report).
problem_entry: Machine-learning optimization problems that are nonlinear, high-dimensional, stochastic, data-heavy and sometimes non-convex; get the benefits of stochastic-gradient and batch methods while avoiding their shortcomings (abstract).
key_idea: Two families: gradient aggregation re-using past gradients (judged on testing, not training, error) and adaptive sampling that reduces gradient noise as optimization progresses; both incorporate curvature even when Hessian estimates use inaccurate gradients (abstract).
experiments: Planned: software implementations tested on realistic machine-learning applications (abstract). Outcomes report: progressive batching tested on realistic applications; DFO methods tested on ML and simulation-based models (NSF outcomes report).
positioning: Grant record (NSF DMS, Computational Mathematics / OE Operations Engineering, $270,000, 08/2016-07/2020); lists outputs Xie-Byrd-Nocedal SIOPT 2019, Berahas-Bollapragada-Nocedal OMS 2020, Bollapragada-Byrd-Nocedal IMA JNA 2018 (NSF record).
writing: Opens with a broad AI / machine-learning impact paragraph before the technical paragraph; the 2020 award (S167) reuses its opening sentence (abstract).
limits_future: Outcomes report (2020): progressive batching designed, implemented, tested and shown convergent; a survey of DFO methods led to gradient estimation inside quasi-Newton rather than grid search or interpolation (NSF outcomes report, paraphrase).

method_links.note: Quasi-Newton engine kept and fed approximate gradients in noisy DFO; curvature updating made robust to inaccurate gradients.
After surveying all existing DFO methods, the dismissed gradient-estimation route was judged more efficient even for noisy systems.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Adaptive sampling to reduce noise in stochastic gradients as optimization progresses; same device in S167.

transferable: When designing an optimizer for learning, state the success criterion as test error rather than training error up front, so the algorithm is designed and judged against it (abstract).
coauthors: none on the record (sole PI); listed outputs with Byrd, Xie, Berahas, Bollapragada

quotes.text: Two families of algorithms will be developed to garner the benefits of both stochastic gradient methods and batch methods, while avoiding their shortcomings.

An important aspect of this research is the design of an efficient strategy for incorporating second-order information that captures curvature of the optimized loss function, even in the case when Hessian estimates are based on inaccurate gradients.

title: Zero-Order and Stochastic Methods for Large-Scale Optimization
contribution: NSF award DMS-2011494 (2020-2024, Nocedal sole PI) for sample-size-controlled methods for stochastic objectives with deterministic constraints and for zero-order noisy methods that pair gradient approximation with quasi-Newton updating; its 2024 outcomes report names design principles for turning classical algorithms into noise-tolerant ones as the likely main contribution (abstract; NSF outcomes report).
problem_entry: Varying-sample-size methods are known for unconstrained problems, but their extension to constraints is not simple because projections or proximal operators introduce discontinuities; plus zero-order methods for noisy unconstrained problems (abstract).
key_idea: Zero-order: invest effort in a good gradient approximation of the noisy function and delegate the quadratic model to quasi-Newton updating instead of interpolation; constrained stochastic: varying sample sizes to reduce gradient variance (abstract).
assumptions: Stochastic objective with deterministic constraints (project 1); noisy unconstrained objective (project 2) (abstract).
experiments: Planned demonstrations on reinforcement-learning problems; the two projects combined are to scale to millions of variables (abstract). Outcomes report: experiments on problems with nonlinear constraints (NSF outcomes report).
positioning: Grant record (NSF DMS Computational Mathematics, $200,000, 08/2020-07/2024); lists Sun & Nocedal, Math. Program. 202 (2023), noisy trust-region method (NSF record).
writing: Reuses and extends the 2016 award's opening sentence (S169), then a technical paragraph built on an explicit contrast with interpolation-based DFO; ends with NSF's standard merit statement (abstract).
limits_future: Outcomes report (2024): the surprising finding that a few design principles transform a classical algorithm into one handling noise, including zero-order, is named the possibly most important long-term contribution (NSF outcomes report, paraphrase).

method_links.note: Gradient approximation feeds classical quasi-Newton updating; the 2024 outcomes report states design principles that turn a classical algorithm into a noisy one (matches the design guidelines of arXiv:2401.15007).
Explicit contrast with interpolation-model DFO in favour of the simpler gradient-approximation + quasi-Newton route.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Varying sample sizes to gradually reduce the variance in the gradient approximation, extended to deterministic constraints; same device as S169.

transferable: Write a one-sentence contrast with the dominant approach that says where the effort goes: unlike [rival class], the proposed methods invest effort in [X] and delegate [Y] to [a classical tool] (abstract).
To extend a technique proven in the unconstrained case, name the specific obstruction (here discontinuities from projections/proximal operators) and make it the research question (abstract).
coauthors: none on the record (sole PI); listed output with Shigeng Sun

quotes.text: Unlike derivative-free methods that construct quadratic models of the objective function using interpolation techniques, the proposed methods invest significant effort in computing a good approximation to the gradient of the noisy function and delegate the construction of a quadratic model to quasi-Newton updating.

they have been studied in the context of unconstrained optimization, but their extension to the constrained setting is not simple because the projections or proximal operators used to enforce the constraints introduce discontinuities.

title: An Iterative Approach for Solving the SCOPF Problem Applying LP, SOCP, and NLP Subproblems
contribution: ARPA-E/OSTI report record (DOE-Northwestern-1077, contract AR0001077) proposing an iterative LP-filtering / SOCP-relaxation / Knitro interior-point approach to security-constrained optimal power flow (abstract; OSTI record).
problem_entry: Efficient algorithms and software for the security-constrained optimal power flow (SCOPF) problem (abstract).
key_idea: (a) linear subproblems and active-set filtering pick the most important contingencies and shrink the model; (b) SOCP relaxations reach the neighbourhood of the global optimum and a lower bound; (c) Artelys Knitro's nonconvex interior-point solver converges to the optimal solution (abstract).
experiments: Planned experiments on the tradeoff between contingency-subproblem complexity and fast solvability; results not read (abstract).
positioning: OSTI record, sponsor USDOE ARPA-E, dated 2024-07-19; linked 4-page PDF headed GO Challenge 1 Final Report, team NU_Columbia_Artelys (OSTI record; PDF p. 1 looked at only to identify it).
writing: Proposal tense: the record text begins with 'We propose' (abstract).

method_links.note: Integrates LP filtering, SOCP relaxation and interior-point NLP in one pipeline, with tradeoffs to be settled by experiment.

transferable: Stage a large nonconvex problem: cheap linear screening to reduce the model, a convex relaxation to land near the global optimum and certify a lower bound, then a local NLP solve to finish (abstract).
coauthors: sole author on the record (Nocedal); PDF team name NU_Columbia_Artelys

quotes.text: use linear subproblems and other active set filtering techniques to identify the most important contingencies and drastically reduce the SCOPF model size
To identify the most effective approach, we will experiment with several techniques to identify the tradeoffs between contingency subproblem complexity and fast solvability.
